title: Upgrading the ladder fixture
intro: Every slot on this page is empty and every one renders a different kind of apparatus, so the probe table has room to climb and room to stall. AcmeDB 2.0 adds online snapshots and renames one config key. The release also retires the v1 wire protocol, which means drivers older than 1.8 can no longer connect at all, and anyone still on the 1.7 line should plan a dump-and-reload window rather than an in-place upgrade. The upgrade matrix below covers the four supported starting points in order, from the common 1.9.x installs that only need the config rename down to the long-unsupported releases where nothing migrates cleanly and a fresh datadir is the honest answer. Snapshots are the headline feature: they run online, they are point-in-time consistent, and they restore without a support ticket, which was the dealbreaker the last time this page's recommendations were reviewed. Cold starts on older databases drop from minutes to seconds once the snapshot catalog is warm, although snapshots of databases over two terabytes still take hours rather than minutes. The remaining sections collect the links, guides, and loose items that did not fit anywhere else on the page.
